next_step: Deliver detailed reserved-capacity cost model and schedule perf POC week of 2026-03-15
notes:
CRM notes: Caldera is a verticalized SaaS for regulated financial analytics; strong interest in Dedicated capacity + VPC private control.

Summary of requirements and asks: 
- Workloads: conversational support agents (chat) + high-volume embeddings and reranking for realtime search. Expect ~150 sustained gen reqs/sec at 1k token avg per request for chat during peak, plus 1M embeddings/day (batchable).
- Latency SLOs: p95 inference <120ms for short-chat turn (<=512 tokens), <250ms for 1k token tails; tail risk is critical.
- Throughput/Capacity: initial reserved plan ~6 H100-equivalent GPUs (80 GB), target burst headroom to 12 GPUs for seasonal peaks. Want autoscale/burst policy and reserved baseline.
- Utilization assumptions: internal ops model assumes 60-75% steady utilization on reserved pool (after prefix caching & batching). finance expects break-even utilization ~50% for 1-year commit, ~40% for 3-year commit due to deeper discounts.
- Cost modeling (high-level supplied in meeting):
   * Hosted baseline (adhoc/onsite VMs): estimated $0.0020 per generated token at current Open / hosted pricing assumptions.
   * Dedicate reserved example (pro-forma): 6x H100 reserved + 6x burst on-demand -> effective unit cost range $0.0006 - $0.0010 per generated token depending on utilization and KV cache hit rate.
   * Embeddings unit: reserved amortized cost ~ $0.00003 per embedding (256-d) at projected 60% GPU util over month.
   * End-to-end blended unit economics (chat + embeddings): conservative blended per-token $0.0009, achievable $0.00065 with model quantization + batching and 70% util.
- SLA negotiations: Caldera legal wants 99.95% uptime, p95 latency SLOs with credits tied to missed targets, 24/7 enterprise support with 1-hour P1 response. They requested explicit rollback/fallback to smaller model variants and documented cold-start guarantees for scaling.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration for model keys, audit log retention 7 years for some flows, EU data residency for a subset of customers (multi-tenant routing).

Recent timeline / interactions: 
- 2026-01-14: Intro call (Maya) — high level requirements, Caldera product execs decided to evaluate dedicated.
- 2026-01-28: Tech deep-dive with SE (Diego) — ran synthetic throughput profile, captured seq-length distribution.
- 2026-02-10: Shared initial cost worksheet (drive/redwood/caldera/cost-model-v1.xlsx).
- 2026-02-17: Fireflies call ff-2026-02-17-1245 — legal & infra participated; Caldera pushed for 3-year commitment discount scenarios.
- 2026-02-25: POC kick-off call (ff-2026-02-25-3312). Diego recommended KV prefix caching and per-route batching for chat.
- 2026-03-02: Internal product Q&A — asked for detailed fallback policy doc and canary rollout schedule.
- 2026-03-03: Sizing workshop — Redwood proposed (6 reserved / 6 burst) H100-equivalent; Caldera engineering asked for cost per token sensitivity table (attached).

POC notes / perf snippets: 
- In early perf runs with 4 GPU equivalent, observed p95 160-210ms for 1k-token synthetic traces; with KV prefix cache enabled p95 dropped to ~110-130ms for common flows.
- Observed batching improved throughput ~2.6x for generation workloads at <10% tail latency cost.
- Embedding batch jobs can be scheduled off-peak and reduce peak commitments by ~18% monthly.

Commercial asks from Caldera: 
- Provide 1-year and 3-year reserved pricing decks with clear utilization breakpoints and example unit economics per token.
- Clear SLA language for latency SLOs + credits tied to p95 misses and availability.
- Migration/runbook for private VPC deployment and key management steps.

Quotes / paraphrases: 
- "We need predictable unit economics — if the math doesn't work at 60% util we can't sign." (VP Eng)
- "Latency tails are our business risk; any missed p95 will be visible to customers." (Head of Product)

Next steps (agreed): 
- Redwood to deliver v2 cost-model and committed capacity options by 2026-03-10 (Maya + Diego).
- Schedule perf POC (2-week) starting 2026-03-15; include production-like traffic replay and residency isolation test.
- Legal to exchange initial SLA redlines (Caldera legal -> Redwood legal) by 2026-03-20.

Open/Blockers: 
- Caldera legal pushed for explicit data residency carve-outs that may require separate private cluster(s).
- Procurement timeline unclear (Q2 procurement freeze possible).
- Need to validate SOC2 gap for one regulated product line.

Recommended Redwood positioning notes for AE/SE: 
- Lead with quantized + batching scenario to show unit-cost delta vs hosted; show sensitivity table at 40/50/60/70% util.
- Emphasize fallback model variants and automated routing to meet latency SLOs while reducing cost.
- Pre-seed SLA compromise: start with 99.9% + latency commitments for core endpoints, escalate to 99.95% once dedicated pool is in steady state.

Attachments / references: cost-model-v2.xlsx (drive link), perf-run-summaries (internal), initial SLA redline (drive/redwood/security/caldera-sla-reqs.docx).
